title: Enhanced Magnetocaloric Properties of the (MnNi)<sub>0.6</sub>Si<sub>0.62</sub>(FeCo)<sub>0.4</sub>Ge<sub>0.38</sub> High-Entropy Alloy Obtained by Co Substitution.

recollection.starting_material: A multi-principal-element Mn–Ni–Si–Fe–Ge alloy similar to earlier MnxNi1−xSi–Ge Heusler-type systems
recollection.intervention: Partial substitution of Co for Fe (or simultaneous Co and Fe incorporation) in the high-entropy alloy composition, followed by arc-melting and possibly annealing, then characterization of magnetic and structural properties
recollection.structure: Single-phase B20/B2 or Heusler-like solid solution with fcc or bcc lattice retaining high configurational entropy; slight lattice shrinkage due to Co incorporation
recollection.mechanism: Co substitution tunes the valence-electron concentration and magnetic exchange, shifting the first-order magnetostructural transition temperature toward room temperature, reducing hysteresis and enhancing magnetic entropy change
recollection.results: Maximum isothermal magnetic-entropy change |ΔS_M| ~ 4-6 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 2 T around 300 K; refrigeration capacity ~ 100-150 J kg⁻¹; thermal hysteresis ≤2 K; coercivity <100 Oe

score.note: The recollection reverses the key substitution site: Co replaces Ni, not Fe. It also misidentifies the Ni2In-type/TiNiSi-type structures as B20/B2 or Heusler-like. The mechanism only generically links Co to magnetic exchange and transition tuning; it misses austenite stabilization and phase-coupled giant magnetocaloric behavior and incorrectly claims strongly reduced hysteresis. Its entropy-change and hysteresis values are far from the reported values.
